newsitem.title: USA: Mitsubishi Motors sees higher U.S. sales.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Motors sees higher U.S. sales.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said Wednesday it expects its U.S. auto sales to be about 235,000 units in 1997, up from 187,126 reported in 1996.
"We're looking to do about 235,000," said Kevin Ormes, group vice president of sales and marketing at Mitsubishi Motor Sales of America Inc, a Mitsubishi Motors unit.
Ormes was speaking to reporters after a presentation at the North American International Auto Show here.

"Most of that big volume will come from our new products," he said, adding that the company expects to sell about 35,000 Montero Sport sports utility vehicle, a lighter version of the company's Montero. The Montero Sport ES, which will be available in March, will be priced at $17,800, he said.
Mitsubishi also expects to sell 12,000-15,000 Diamante sedans and 12,000-18,000 Mirage subcompact models.
In terms of production, Mistubishi can add about five-10 percent more production in the United States, where it makes the Eclipse sports coupe and Galant mid-sized sedan.
Ormes also said Mitsubishi's "Built for Living" advertising campaign, begun last year, has shown results.
While he did not have specific figures, there has been increased awareness in Mitsubishi and increased interest in buying the Japanese automaker's vehicles in the United States, he said.
"We're getting on people's shopping lists," he said.
In its 15th year selling automobiles in the United States, Mitsubishi now also offers a full product line, Ormes noted.
"We were really more of a niche marketer in the beginning and now we're able to fill out the entire product line," he said.
